the extracellular domain of CD8beta can independently interact with MHC class Ib2m and may also stabilize interaction between MHC class I/CD8alpha and MHC class I/IgG FcRgamma.

(1) the extracellular domain of CD8beta interacts with MHC class Ib2m dimers and may enhance CD8alpha-mediated interaction with MHC; and (2) the extracellular portion CD8beta may be uniquely capable of efficient coupling of the TCR/ CD3 complex with other surface components capable enhancing TCR-mediated signaling.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the CD8 coreceptor function in the TCR/ CD3 complex and its role in T cell responses.
the molecular mechanisms by which CD8alpha and CD8beta subunits mediate their effects on T cell function.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms of CD8-mediated T cell response modulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD8beta is not simply a CD8alpha subunit that is incapable of associating with the TCR, but is a subunit capable of independent interaction and coupling to the TCR/TCR complex.
CD8beta is a coreceptor capable of enhancing T cell responses to MHC class I ligands, and this function is at least partially mediated through its extracellular portion.
CD8beta is a coreceptor for TCR-mediated signals and that the extracellular domain is the major functional domain of CD8beta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extracellular domain of CD8beta can independently interact with MHC class 1/beta2m and TCR/CD 3 and may also enhance interaction between CD8alpha and MHC class I.
CD8alpha and CD8beta have distinct functions in T cell responses, and that these functions are not necessarily mediated by the same mechanisms.
CD8beta may be capable of interacting with multiple components of the immune synapse to influence the outcome of antigen recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CD8alpha and CD8beta subunits are capable of mediating unique and complementary effects on T cell responses, and that CD8beta may be uniquely capable of mediating the interaction with the T cell receptor and coupling it to other surface components.
the CD8beta molecule can independently and efficiently interact with MHC class 1 and the TCR/ CD3 complex.
CD8beta can function as a coreceptor independently from CD8alpha.
